text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 2.8% today, bouncing back after a brutal week that saw the stock drop nearly 7% since late October. The bounce came as U.S. crude oil fell more than 3% on Monday following reports of U.S.-Iran diplomatic efforts, which normally would hurt a refiner—but the move appears driven by relief that tensions may ease rather than collapse further, plus a company leadership change and strategic update announced on October 29th that may have signaled confidence to investors.

The broader picture matters here: oil prices have swung wildly this week on geopolitical news (Qatari mediators in Tehran, talk of avoiding additional strikes), and refineries are running at 92.8% capacity with healthy crude and product inventories. The stock's weak two-week performance likely reflects investor caution ahead of Big Oil earnings, where guidance—not just profits—will determine whether refiners can weather the uncertainty around oil prices and Middle East tensions.
